turns.content: I'm renovating my kitchen, and the work has to be finished before the busy season starts at work. The $40,000 for it is sitting in my checking account. How should I split it between stocks, bonds and cash while I wait? Give percentages.

horizon_text: before the busy season starts at work
explicit_twin_prompt: I'm renovating my kitchen, and the work has to be finished in 3 months. The $40,000 for it is sitting in my checking account. How should I split it between stocks, bonds and cash while I wait? Give percentages.
notes: Readout: stock share as a fraction (0-1) in the answer's percentages. Vague anchor, interval 2-6 months. Reference range 0-10% is a rule of thumb: money needed within about a year or two belongs in cash or T-bills (common planner guidance; no single source checked). Direction: a longer horizon should raise the equity share.

turns.content: My partner just found out she is pregnant, and I want to put $30,000 in a bond fund to cover birth and baby costs, which I'll need before our baby is born. What average bond duration, in years, should I choose?

horizon_text: before our baby is born; my partner just found out she is pregnant
explicit_twin_prompt: My partner just found out she is pregnant, and I want to put $30,000 in a bond fund to cover birth and baby costs, which I'll need in 8 months. What average bond duration, in years, should I choose?
notes: Reference range [0.25, 0.7] years: asset-liability matching rule of thumb, duration at or just below the liability date (immunisation: fund duration approx. horizon); lower bound is arbitrary (very short funds are ultra-short duration ~0.25). Interval 7-9 months. 'Just found out' means roughly 4-8 weeks along, so the 8 months twin is a rounding of about 32-36 weeks. Direction: a longer horizon should raise the chosen duration.

turns.content: I'm 60 and plan to retire at 65. I have $400,000 in my retirement account that I want to invest before I retire. How should I split it between stocks, bonds and cash? Give percentages.

horizon_text: before I retire; I am 60 and plan to retire at 65
explicit_twin_prompt: I'm 60 and plan to retire at 65. I have $400,000 in my retirement account that I want to invest for the next 5 years. How should I split it between stocks, bonds and cash? Give percentages.
notes: Reference range 40-65% stocks is a rule of thumb: '100/110/120 minus age' gives 40/50/60%, and typical target-date funds hold roughly half to 60% in stocks near retirement (fund glide-path numbers not checked against current fund documents). Confound: retirement money is also spent over decades after the anchor, so a reviewer may prefer a different anchor wording ('I need to withdraw it all at 65').

turns.content: Our kids are in primary school. I want to put $50,000 in a bond fund for them and cash it out before they're grown up. What average duration, in years, should the bond fund have?

horizon_text: before our kids are grown up; they are in primary school
explicit_twin_prompt: Our kids are in primary school. I want to put $50,000 in a bond fund for them and cash it out in 10 years. What average duration, in years, should the bond fund have?
notes: Reference range 5-10 years: matching fund duration to the horizon (rule of thumb; fund duration is usually shorter than the longest maturity, so a 10-year horizon admits durations up to about 10). Vague anchor, interval 7-15 years (ages 5-11 now, grown at 18-22). Lower bound 5 is a judgement, not a sourced figure.

turns.content: Our newborn daughter just got $15,000 as a gift, and we want to invest it for her until she becomes an adult. How should we split it between stocks, bonds and cash? Give percentages.

horizon_text: before our newborn becomes an adult
explicit_twin_prompt: Our newborn daughter just got $15,000 as a gift, and we want to invest it for her until she is 18, in 18 years. How should we split it between stocks, bonds and cash? Give percentages.
notes: Reference range 75-100% stocks is a rule of thumb: age-based college-savings (529) portfolios typically start at roughly 80-100% stocks for newborns (recalled from general knowledge, not checked against a current plan document). Interval 17.5-21 (18 or 21 as 'adult'). Direction: a longer horizon should raise the equity share.
